title: Saddle / Inside Sankaku
description: A strong leg entanglement around the hip line and knee line, often carrying heel-hook danger when the heel is exposed.
topPlayerGoals: The top player wants to control Saddle / Inside Sankaku through head position, inside position, and directed pressure.
The attacker wants to isolate the knee line, secondary leg, and heel exposure.
Keep a stable base so you are not off-balanced or countered.
bottomPlayerGoals: The bottom player wants to survive Saddle / Inside Sankaku with frames, pummeling, or the right angle.
The defender wants to hide the heel, free the secondary leg, and clear the knee line.
Recognize danger signals early instead of waiting for the position to settle.
controlPoints: Main control point: Trapped knee line, heel exposure, and hip rotation..
Head, hands, hips, and knees should share the same force direction.
The elbow-knee connection or hip-shoulder line determines whether the position is still alive or already locked.
escapePriorities: Escape priority: Do not spin blindly into rotational pressure..
Protect the neck, back, knee line, or arm line before countering.
If inside position is lost, reset one defensive layer first.

advancementOptions.action: Free the knee line before turning
advancementOptions.why: This is the natural branch when you win the main control point and the opponent is forced to defend.

dangerSignals: The chin or neck is pulled out of a safe line.
The elbow separates from the ribs or knee.
The hip line is locked while the shoulder line is still being pulled.
You need a long hand post to avoid falling.
